metadata.title: QLORA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs

problem.value: Finetuning very large language models is prohibitively expensive in terms of GPU memory.

evidence.quote: However, finetuning very large models is prohibitively expensive; regular 16-bit finetuning of a LLaMA 65B parameter model [57] requires more than 780 GB of GPU memory.

problem.value: Existing quantization methods only work for inference and fail during training.

evidence.quote: While recent quantization methods can reduce the memory footprint of LLMs [14,13,18,66], such techniques only work for inference and break down during training [65].

contributions.value: Introduction of 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4), an information-theoretically optimal data type for normally distributed weights.

evidence.quote: QLORA introduces a number of innovations to save memory without sacrificing performance: (a) 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4), a new data type that is information theoretically optimal for normally distributed weights

contributions.value: Double Quantization to reduce the average memory footprint by quantizing the quantization constants.

evidence.quote: (b) Double Quantization to reduce the average memory footprint by quantizing the quantization constants, and (c) Paged Optimizers to manage memory spikes.

contributions.value: Paged Optimizers to manage memory spikes.

evidence.quote: (b) Double Quantization to reduce the average memory footprint by quantizing the quantization constants, and (c) Paged Optimizers to manage memory spikes.

task.value: instruction following and chatbot performance evaluation

evidence.quote: We use QLORA to finetune more than 1,000 models, providing a detailed analysis of instruction following and chatbot performance across 8 instruction datasets, multiple model types (LLaMA, T5), and model scales that would be infeasible to run with regular finetuning (e.g. 33B and 65B parameter models).

method_summary.value: QLORA utilizes a 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) storage data type for base model weights and a BFloat16 data type for computations, dequantizing weights to 16-bit for matrix multiplication during forward and backward passes.

evidence.quote: QLORA has one low-precision storage data type, in our case usually 4-bit, and one computation data type that is usually BFloat16.

method_summary.value: Double Quantization is applied to the quantization constants to further reduce their memory footprint by treating them as inputs to a second quantization step.

evidence.quote: More specifically, Double Quantization treats quantization constants c 2 FP32 of the first quantization as inputs to a second quantization.

method_summary.value: Paged Optimizers are employed using NVIDIA unified memory to automatically page optimizer states between GPU and CPU RAM, preventing out-of-memory errors during gradient checkpointing spikes.

evidence.quote: Paged Optimizers use the NVIDIA unified memoryfoot_0 feature wich does automatic page-to-page transfers between the CPU and GPU for error-free GPU processing in the scenario where the GPU occasionally runs out-of-memory.

method_summary.value: The approach integrates Low-rank Adapters (LoRA) where only the adapter parameters receive weight gradients while the base model weights remain fixed and quantized.

evidence.quote: To summarize, QLORA has one storage data type (usually 4-bit NormalFloat) and a computation data type .

novelty.value: The introduction of the 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) data type, which is information-theoretically optimal for zero-centered normally distributed weights.

evidence.quote: QLORA achieves high-fidelity 4-bit finetuning via two techniques we propose-4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) quantization and Double Quantization.

novelty.value: The use of Double Quantization to reduce the memory overhead introduced by quantization constants.

evidence.quote: Additionally, we introduce Paged Optimizers, to prevent memory spikes during gradient checkpointing from causing out-of-memory errors that have traditionally made finetuning on a single machine difficult for large models.

novelty.value: The employment of Paged Optimizers to manage memory spikes and prevent out-of-memory errors during single-machine large model finetuning.

evidence.quote: Additionally, we introduce Paged Optimizers, to prevent memory spikes during gradient checkpointing from causing out-of-memory errors that have traditionally made finetuning on a single machine difficult for large models.

seeds_and_runs.value: Repeated tournament procedure 10,000 times with different random seeds

evidence.quote: Similar to Chiang et al. [10], we repeat this procedure 10,000 times with different random seeds to control for ordering effects, e.g., the effect of which model pairs compete with each other first.

ablations.value: Ablation subsampling large datasets into sizes of 50,000, 100,000 and 150,000 to examine quality vs size

evidence.quote: To understand the effects of dataset quality vs. dataset size, we experiment with subsampling large datasets with at least 150,000 samples (Chip2, FLAN v2, Unnatural Instructions), into datasets of size 50,000, 100,000 and 150,000 and examine the resulting trends, as shown in Table 11.

limitations.value: Inability to establish that QLORA matches full 16-bit finetuning at 33B and 65B scales due to resource costs.

evidence.quote: Despite this evidence, we did not establish that QLORA can match full 16-bit finetuning performance at 33B and 65B scales.

limitations.value: Lack of evaluation on other benchmarks such as BigBench, RAFT, and HELM.

evidence.quote: While we provide evaluations on MMLU, the Vicuna benchmark, and the OA benchmark, we did not evaluate on other benchmarks such as BigBench, RAFT, and HELM, and it is not ensured that our evaluations generalize to these benchmarks.

limitations.value: Only a limited responsible AI evaluation of Guanaco was conducted.

evidence.quote: While we provide a detailed evaluation for general chatbot performance, another limitation is that we only do a limited responsible AI evaluation of Guanaco.

limitations.value: Failure to evaluate different bit-precisions like 3-bit base models or different adapter methods.

evidence.quote: An additional limitation is that we did not evaluate different bit-precisions, such as using 3-bit base models, or different adapter methods.

future_work.value: Future work should use HC and Psychology to address subjective preferences in chatbot evaluation.

evidence.quote: Future work should investigate approaches to mitigate these problems drawing from disciplines that developed mechanisms to deal with subjective preferences, such as Human-Computer Interaction and Psychology.

future_work.value: Future work should examine potential biases in automated evaluation systems and mitigation strategies.

evidence.quote: Future work should examine the presence of potential biases in automated evaluation systems as well as possible mitigation strategies.

evidence.quote: We leave it to future work to investigate the degree to which such multilingual training improves performance on instructions in languages other than English and whether this explains the larger gap between Vicuna-13B model (only trained on English data) and Guanaco 33B and 65B on the OA benchmark.

future_work.value: Further study the performance matching at 33B and 65B scales compared to full 16-bit finetuning.

evidence.quote: Due to the immense resource costs, we leave this study to future work.

ethics.value: Finetuning is a dual-use technology that can be abused to cause harm.

evidence.quote: However, finetuning is a dual-use technology that can be abused to cause harm.

ethics.value: Equalizing access to LLM technology allows for better and more independent analysis.

evidence.quote: Widespread use of LLMs has known dangers [8,6], but we believe that equalizing access to a technology that is quickly becoming ubiquitous will allow for better more independent analysis than keeping the power of LLMs in the hands of large corporations that do not release models or source code for auditing.

ethics.value: QLORA may enable privacy-preserving usage of LLMs on devices like mobile phones.

evidence.quote: QLORA can help enable privacy-preserving usage of LLMs, where users can own and manage their own data and models, while simultaneously making LLMs easier to deploy.

claims.value: The best model family, Guanaco, reaches 99.3% of ChatGPT's performance level on the Vicuna benchmark with 24 hours of finetuning.

evidence.quote: Our best model family, which we name Guanaco, outperforms all previous openly released models on the Vicuna benchmark, reaching 99.3% of the performance level of ChatGPT while only requiring 24 hours of finetuning on a single GPU.

claims.value: QLORA reduces average memory requirements for finetuning a 65B model from over 780 GB to under 48 GB.

evidence.quote: QLORA reduces the average memory requirements of finetuning a 65B parameter model from >780GB of GPU memory to <48GB without degrading the runtime or predictive performance compared to a 16bit fully finetuned baseline.
